_readme: THE PAYWALL-FLIP CHECKLIST — every precondition of turning `paywall.enabled` to true for an app in services/platform/src/app-config-data.json. Row AB-M2-01 (full-review round 2, 2026-09-29).

READ by tooling/ci/assert-paywall-flip-ready.mjs, which exits 1 while ANY app whose served config says `paywall.enabled: true` has a precondition here with `open: true` that applies to it (`apps` names the app, or is ["*"]). With every app's paywall off the guard passes and prints what is still open.

A precondition is CLOSED only with `verify`: repo-relative paths, each of which must exist in the tree — the test, guard or record that proves it. Closing a row by editing this file alone, with no evidence path, is refused.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT SEE: the KV override services/platform/src/config.ts lets an operator set at runtime. That switch is owner-gated, and this list is what the owner reads before touching it.
ADD a row when a new precondition is found; never delete one — close it, with its evidence.

preconditions.what: A real Paddle subscription.canceled (no period) ends access and records a revocation, instead of 503 on every delivery.
An approved refund or chargeback stays revoked: a later subscription.updated for the paid-back period does not re-grant.
POST /v1/plan/cancel carries out a Paddle cancel at the period end, and answers a store row with the store's page instead of a false 'provider_not_configured'.

The app picks the cancel path from where the person paid (the entitlement's provider/store), maps the server's 409 to a store outcome with its own copy, and a 404 to 'no active plan' (moneyflows MF-3b). Needs new strings in apps/subscriptiontracker/lib/l10n/app_{en,ta}.arb.
preconditions.closedBy: train st-money-ready (2026-10-01): BillingSource reads the entitlement's store; Manage plan shows 'Manage in {store}' and no Cancel for a store plan; DioCancellationTransport reads 404 as no plan and 409 as CancellationOutcome.inStore.

preconditions.what: One signed purchase per rail unlocks is_pro for its payer through GET /v1/entitlements, and not for anyone else.
DELETE /v1/account cancels a live Paddle subscription before erasure, or refuses with a sentence when it cannot.

The delete-account dialog says what happens to billing (Paddle cancelled at period end; an App Store / Google Play subscription must be cancelled in the store), in en and ta, and shows the sentence the server's 503 `subscription_still_billing` carries in `message`.
preconditions.closedBy: train st-money-ready (2026-10-01): the dialog draws the plan line by where the plan was bought BEFORE the confirm, and the 503's `message` (ApiException.serverSentence → AccountDeletionFailure.serverSentence) is rendered by the login screen's deletion notice, where the sign-out redirect lands the user (review 1 of #1114: the dialog is torn down by that redirect), and cleared on Dismiss.

preconditions.what: A hosted channel (web, windows-store, windows-direct, linux-snap, linux-appimage) can START a checkout from the served config: the hosted rail asks POST /v1/checkout (which attributes the transaction to the verified account) and opens the checkout_url it returns. Before: it required a checkout_url_template that no config serves, so canStartCheckout was false everywhere.

POST /v1/checkout is bounded: CHECKOUT_CEILING_LIMITER (edge, fails open) and CHECKOUT_USER_LIMITER (per verified user, fails closed) are bound at the top level and in env.sandbox, each on its own namespace id.
A store-receipt rail cannot be configured while nothing revokes a bundle_grants row.

A renewal / end-of-trial notice reaches the buyer through a declared medium before a 30-day trial renews (the offerings carry trial_days 30). tooling/ci/assert-purchase-path.mjs refuses the flip without `renewal_notice` on the config contract.
RevenueCat leg (a): a signed store build completes a sandbox purchase and the webhook grants through POST /v1/money/revenuecat (waits on A-20, a signed Apple build).
Every rail the app sells on has an end-to-end sandbox purchase proof: purchase, entitlement flip, feature unlock (e2e legs purchase-sandbox, entitlement-flip, feature-unlock).
Every served offering's price is read back from each rail's own dashboard/API and matches app-config-data.json `prices` (no price is trusted from our copy alone).
The Paddle cancel call (lib/mor/paddle-cancel.ts) is exercised once against a Paddle sandbox subscription and the terminal subscription.canceled is seen to end access.

FullShot can link an account before it is sold: some extension store channel row in tooling/channel-register.json carries a non-null extensionRedirectUri, so POST /v1/ext/codes can mint a code and Pro can become true. Until then a buyer pays for a Pro the extension can never show. assert-paywall-flip-ready.mjs refuses this row CLOSED while every such row is null (contracts/legal/pro-gate.mjs canSignIn).
preconditions.blockedOn: O-EXTENSION-ACCOUNT-CHECK-UNBUILT: every extension channel's extensionRedirectUri is null

preconditions.what: POST /v1/plan/cancel accepts every product POST /v1/checkout sells, so an extension bought on the web is cancelled as easily as it was bought ([5]M-9). Held as a mechanism: the parity test reads both routes' answers over every registered product id.

The checkout compares the account behind the Upgrade URL's link id with the signed-in web user before it charges. Today nothing reads link (sites/nikatru/pricing.html reads app only, and no route takes it), so a web session signed in as account A can pay while the extension is linked to account B, which never becomes Pro.
